1.2::miv4t::, 0.8::quasarcake::

Character 1 occupies the upper-left of the square composition, with his reaching hand nearer to the viewer at the center. His torso remains joined to that arm and continues out of the lower-left crop. His face and reaching hand are the focal points of the figure: the hat frames the face without dwarfing it, and the cloak stays behind his shoulders instead of forming an oversized bright flag across the upper-right half. He releases three small black spell cards toward a fiery vortex inside the lower-right quadrant. Its hot core remains visibly inside the image, separated from the bottom and right edges by dark background. The cards recede along a diagonal into that core, their edges burning away. Two broad orange-gold bands curl inward around the small ivory core, forming a readable spiral; one outer surge then rises along the right side. Dark gaps separate the curved bands. The core is a small concentrated hot point rather than a large radial white explosion. The surge lights only the lower-facing edges of his fingers and cheek and pulls the cloak along its flow. The reflected warmth does not recolor the whole hand; the large robe and cloak shadows stay matte and subdued.

1.3::opaque broad color masses, clear shadow planes, grouped hair locks, principal cloth folds::, matte painting, selective facial detail. Resolve the eyes, glasses and finger gesture selectively. Most hair and cloth surfaces use connected color planes with only a few wide directional swipes, not narrow outlined strips or continuous silky highlights. Keep dark surfaces quiet. The background is one continuous abstract field of ink blue and charcoal violet, painted edge to edge behind the figure and eruption. Volcanic pressure is expressed through dark color layers and fire; there is no visible paper surface, inset rectangular painting, frame or separate blank region.

painterly, sketch, visible brush strokes, loose hand-painted texture, broken edges, blocky volume modeling.

A complete illustration with the freshness of a painted sketch, not an unfinished draft. Directional light separates the principal light and shadow planes without long smooth reflective gradients. Build volumes from confident planes of light and shadow with visible brush edges, with handmade brush edges inside the illustration. The dark background covers the entire canvas and reaches all four image edges without unpainted margins. Use broad flowing paint masses, dry uneven strokes, and crisp small highlights appropriate to each material. Vary the brush size and edge sharpness between different materials. Preserve deliberate brush marks instead of smoothing every surface.
